90	## 1. ADJUDICATION A — the dictionary consumption and the off-overlap question (I-0186 item 2 × I-0182)
91	
92	**Question.** Does DD-R consume the one-sided field dictionary {backward map `hsurj` +
93	`divFamDivisor_injective`} with P-fib's divisor normalized off the chart overlap
94	`π⁻¹(Gm)`, or must the general-MV `hdeg` brick be funded?
95	
96	**Verdict: NEITHER. (i) The off-overlap normalization is mathematically unavailable,
97	and (ii) DD-R consumes neither `hsurj` nor `hdeg` — the universal-family architecture
98	replaces the dictionary consumption entirely.** The I-0182 one-sided-dictionary route
99	is hereby SUPERSEDED for DD-R (it remains correct as a statement about the field
100	dictionary; its consumer is DAT-B, see the boundary flag below).
101	
102	**(i) Evidence that off-overlap support cannot be arranged.** P-fib's `D` is the
103	modulus itself, not an auxiliary choice: in `existsUnique_effective_divisor_of_carve`
104	(`PFib.lean:241`) the divisor is *defined* as `D := Scheme.baseDivisor K KM (M•F)`
105	(`PFib.lean:282`) — the base divisor of the *given* window — and the uniqueness clause
106	pins it pointwise by `baseDivisorAt_normalization` (`:127`): the F1 "normalization"
107	normalizes the *window relative to `D`* (no residual base point), never `D`'s support.
108	As the carve point varies over `Z(♦)`, `D` ranges over **every** effective degree-`g`
109	divisor — the ⟸ direction (DD-4 §2.3) embeds `g·x` for every closed `x`, including
110	`x ∈ π⁻¹(Gm)` = the nonempty chart overlap (`relCover`/`pullbackProd`,
111	`RelativeTwoCover.lean:128`; nonemptiness per I-0186). There is no translation (the
112	curve has no group structure) and no rescale (unit rescaling of `K_M` fixes `bd`).
113	I-0186 item 2 is answered: **NO — P-fib's divisor cannot be arranged off-overlap.**
114	
115	**(ii) Why DD-R nevertheless needs no dictionary.** DD-R's backward direction is
116	*pullback of a universal certified family* constructed over `Z(♦)`'s charts by local
117	generators from the universal carve pair (worksheet §3.4.1) — the equations are window
118	*achievers*, never `pointEquations` products; `divFamOfDivisor` appears nowhere. The
119	only degree identity DD-R needs is fibrewise, **for carve-certified families only**,
120	and it closes without Mayer–Vietoris by the **certified-degree pinch** (DDR-2 below):
121	at a field point, `K_M = H⁰(MF − D_F)` (the sections dictionary, DD-4 Task 5's field
122	content) with corank `g` in `H_M`; the section bound
123	(`h0_divisorSheaf_le_max_of_h0_one`, SectionBound:248) forces `deg D_F ≤ 2g` (the F1
124	move, exactly as `PFib.lean:294–303`); then the exact normalization window
125	(`rank_normalization`, WindowLedger:396, licensed at `deg ≤ 2g` by
126	`two_mul_genus_le_M_mul_windowδ`, WindowLedgerF3:102) gives
127	`r_M − g = h⁰(MF − D_F) = Mδ − deg D_F + 1 − g`, i.e. `deg D_F = g`. No adaptation
128	independence, no inclusion–exclusion, no `hdeg`. I-0179's wall is not touched.
129	
130	**The EXACT hypotheses DD-R's bricks carry**: `adaptation.IsCertified g` plus carve
131	membership (the pair `ε(F)` satisfies `(♦)`, corank exactly `g`) — never a support
132	condition `supp D ∩ π⁻¹(Gm) = ∅`, never `hdeg`, never `hsurj`. Any DD-R prover writing
133	a support-separation hypothesis (`hsep`, `subsingleton_ovlColength_of_sep`) has left
134	the route: those belong to the *separated field kit* (DivisorFamilyFieldDegree), which
135	DD-R does not consume.

138	`divFamFieldEquiv` (and hence `hsurj` for arbitrary — including overlap-supported —
139	divisors) is DAT-B's consumption surface (worksheet §4.2 row), and I-0186's obstruction

10	/-!
11	# DDR-3 — the relative local-generator construction (`informal/spec-dd-r.md` §3 item 3)
12	
13	Kleiman `lm:ctn` (ii)⟹(iii)⟹(i) on the relative curve `C_R = relCurve C R` over a
14	Noetherian test ring `R` (the `Z(♦)`-chart rings): from a **theta generator seed** — a
15	choice, at every point `z` of `C_R`, of a pinned chart side, a basic-open neighbourhood
16	piece, and a section of a submodule `K ⊆ H⁰(𝒪(Θᵃ))` whose chart component *generates the
17	subsheaf `K·𝒪` on the piece* (`IsGenerator.dvd`, the Nakayama-neighbourhood clause) and is
18	*fibrewise regular* (`IsGenerator.fibre_regular`, the P-fib input at every `κ(p)`) — this
19	file constructs a `LocalEquations` system with a `DivisorAdaptation` refining it:
20	
21	The flatness ladder and the side-uniform theta components live in
22	`AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivSchemeFamilySide`; this file assembles them:
23	
24	* `AlgebraicGeometry.ThetaGeneratorSeed`, `ThetaGeneratorSeed.IsGenerator` — the seed and
25	  the two `lm:ctn` clauses, stated so that the fibrewise inputs are exactly what P-fib at
26	  `κ(p)` produces (spec §7 risk 2: one named boundary for the DD-4 transport seam);
27	* `ThetaGeneratorSeed.res_eqn_mem_nonZeroDivisors` /
28	  `ThetaGeneratorSeed.germ_eqn_mem_nonZeroDivisors` — **the germ-regularity law**
29	  ((iii)⟹(i)): fibrewise-regular + flat ⟹ regular, through
30	  `Module.Flat.mem_nonZeroDivisors_of_forall_tmul_residueField` on the basic-open
31	  section rings;
32	* `ThetaGeneratorSeed.exists_ratioUnit` — the overlap units: two local generators of the
33	  same subsheaf `K·𝒪` divide each other, and mutual divisibility against a regular
34	  section is a unit ratio;
35	* `ThetaGeneratorSeed.localEquations` / `ThetaGeneratorSeed.divisorAdaptation` — **the
36	  DDR-3 deliverable**: the local-equation system of the seed and a finite chart
37	  adaptation refining it (through the `exists_divisorAdaptation` extraction — no anchor
38	  field of `DivisorAdaptation` is consumed, per the DD-2 carrier-surgery freeze);
39	* `ThetaGeneratorSeed.le_vanishingSubmodule` — **the divisibility law for DDR-4/DDR-5**:
40	  `K ⊆ H⁰(𝒪(Θᵃ − d))` for the constructed system `d` (every element of `K` vanishes
41	  along `d`, germwise).
42	
43	The construction of a seed from the universal carve pair (P-fib achiever choice at each
44	`κ(p)` + `exists_fibrewise_tmul_ne_zero_of_projective`) is the gated follow-up recorded
45	in the DDR-3 lane memory; it consumes `RiemannRoch/DegreeBaseFieldInvariance` and the
46	DD-4 base-field-transport seam and produces exactly a `ThetaGeneratorSeed` with
47	`IsGenerator`.
48	-/
49	
50	set_option autoImplicit false
51	set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false
52	
53	universe u
54	
55	open CategoryTheory TopologicalSpace Opposite
56	open scoped TensorProduct
57	
58	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
59	
60	attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra
61	
62	
63	/-! ## The theta generator seed and the `lm:ctn` clauses -/
64	
65	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
66	variable {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [Algebra k R]
67	variable {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsFinite π] {a : ℕ}
68	
69	/-- **A theta generator seed for a submodule `K ⊆ H⁰(𝒪(Θᵃ))`** (worksheet §3.4.1): at
70	every point `z` of the relative curve, a pinned chart side containing `z`, a basic-open
71	neighbourhood piece `D(h z)` of the chart, and a global section `sec z ∈ K` — the
72	candidate local generator.  The two `lm:ctn` clauses on a seed are
73	`ThetaGeneratorSeed.IsGenerator`. -/
74	structure ThetaGeneratorSeed (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) (R : Type u) [CommRing R]
75	    [Algebra k R] (π : C.left ⟶ P1 k) [IsFinite π] (a : ℕ)
76	    (K : Submodule R (relThetaSections C R π a)) : Type u where
77	  /-- The pinned chart side of the piece at `z`. -/
78	  side : relCurve C R → Bool
79	  /-- The basic-open generator of the piece at `z`. -/
80	  h : ∀ z : relCurve C R, Γ(relCurve C R, relPinnedChart C R π (side z))
81	  /-- The point lies in its piece. -/
82	  mem_basicOpen : ∀ z : relCurve C R, z ∈ (relCurve C R).basicOpen (h z)
83	  /-- The candidate local generator at `z`. -/
84	  sec : relCurve C R → relThetaSections C R π a
85	  /-- The candidate generators are drawn from `K`. -/
86	  sec_mem : ∀ z, sec z ∈ K
87	
88	namespace ThetaGeneratorSeed
89	
90	variable {K : Submodule R (relThetaSections C R π a)} (D : ThetaGeneratorSeed C R π a K)
91	
92	/-- The neighbourhood piece at `z`: the basic open `D(h z)` of the pinned chart. -/
93	noncomputable def piece (z : relCurve C R) : (relCurve C R).Opens :=
94	  (relCurve C R).basicOpen (D.h z)
95	
96	lemma mem_piece (z : relCurve C R) : z ∈ D.piece z := D.mem_basicOpen z
97	
98	lemma piece_le (z : relCurve C R) : D.piece z ≤ relPinnedChart C R π (D.side z) :=
99	  (relCurve C R).basicOpen_le (D.h z)
100	
101	/-- The pieces are affine (basic opens of the affine pinned charts). -/
102	lemma isAffineOpen_piece (z : relCurve C R) : IsAffineOpen (D.piece z) :=
103	  (isAffineOpen_relPinnedChart C R π (D.side z)).basicOpen (D.h z)
104	
105	/-- **Flatness of the piece sections over the test ring** (the (iii)⟹(i) licence). -/
106	theorem flat_sections_piece (z : relCurve C R) :
107	    Module.Flat R Γ(relCurve C R, D.piece z) :=
108	  flat_sections_basicOpen R (isAffineOpen_relPinnedChart C R π (D.side z))
109	    (flat_sections_relPinnedChart C R π (D.side z)) (D.h z)
110	
111	/-- **The candidate local equation at `z`**: the side component of the chosen generator,
112	restricted to the piece. -/
113	noncomputable def eqn (z : relCurve C R) : Γ(relCurve C R, D.piece z) :=
114	  relThetaResSide a (D.side z) (D.piece_le z) (D.sec z)
115	
116	/-- **The `lm:ctn` clauses on a seed** (Kleiman (ii)⟹(iii) packaged as its output, plus
117	the fibrewise-regularity input of (iii)⟹(i)):
118	
119	* `dvd` — the chosen generator generates the subsheaf `K·𝒪` on its piece: the side
120	  component of every element of `K` is a multiple of the equation (the Nakayama
121	  neighbourhood clause, produced fibrewise by the P-fib achiever +
122	  `exists_fibrewise_tmul_ne_zero_of_projective`);
123	* `fibre_regular` — the equation is a nonzerodivisor in every residue-field fibre of
124	  every basic sub-open of the piece (produced by P-fib: the fibre of the equation is a
125	  nonzero section of an integral curve over `κ(p)`).
126	
127	Both clauses are stated relative to the test ring only, so the DD-4 base-field-transport
128	seam moves a single boundary (spec-dd-r §7 risk 2). -/
129	structure IsGenerator : Prop where
130	  dvd : ∀ (z : relCurve C R) ⦃ψ : relThetaSections C R π a⦄, ψ ∈ K →
131	    relThetaResSide a (D.side z) (D.piece_le z) ψ ∈ Ideal.span {D.eqn z}
132	  fibre_regular : ∀ (z : relCurve C R) (p : PrimeSpectrum R)
133	      (f : Γ(relCurve C R, D.piece z)),
134	    ((relCurve C R).resHom ((relCurve C R).basicOpen_le f) (D.eqn z) ⊗ₜ[R]
135	        (1 : p.asIdeal.ResidueField)) ∈
136	      nonZeroDivisors
137	        (Γ(relCurve C R, (relCurve C R).basicOpen f) ⊗[R] p.asIdeal.ResidueField)
138	
139	variable {D}
140	
141	/-! ### The germ-regularity law ((iii)⟹(i): fibrewise-regular + flat ⟹ regular) -/
142	
143	/-- **Section-level regularity on basic sub-opens of the piece**: the restriction of the
144	equation to any basic open `D(f) ⊆ D(h z)` is a nonzerodivisor — the slicing criterion
145	`Module.Flat.mem_nonZeroDivisors_of_forall_tmul_residueField` over the Noetherian test
146	ring, fed by the seed's fibrewise regularity. -/
147	theorem res_eqn_mem_nonZeroDivisors [IsNoetherianRing R] (hD : D.IsGenerator)
148	    (z : relCurve C R) (f : Γ(relCurve C R, D.piece z)) :
149	    (relCurve C R).resHom ((relCurve C R).basicOpen_le f) (D.eqn z)
150	      ∈ nonZeroDivisors Γ(relCurve C R, (relCurve C R).basicOpen f) := by
151	  haveI : Module.Flat R Γ(relCurve C R, (relCurve C R).basicOpen f) :=
152	    flat_sections_basicOpen R (D.isAffineOpen_piece z) (D.flat_sections_piece z) f
153	  exact Module.Flat.mem_nonZeroDivisors_of_forall_tmul_residueField
154	    (fun p => hD.fibre_regular z p f)
155	
156	/-- **The germ-regularity law** ((iii)⟹(i), the `LocalEquations.regular` clause): every
157	germ of the equation on its piece is a nonzerodivisor.  A zerodivisor relation at the
158	stalk descends to a basic sub-open of the piece, where the flat slicing criterion
159	applies. -/
160	theorem germ_eqn_mem_nonZeroDivisors [IsNoetherianRing R] (hD : D.IsGenerator)
161	    (z : relCurve C R) {y : relCurve C R} (hy : y ∈ D.piece z) :
162	    ((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ (D.piece z) y hy).hom (D.eqn z)
163	      ∈ nonZeroDivisors ((relCurve C R).presheaf.stalk y) := by
164	  rw [mem_nonZeroDivisors_iff_right]
165	  intro τ hτ
166	  obtain ⟨V', hyV', t, ht⟩ := (relCurve C R).presheaf.exists_germ_eq τ
167	  -- push the product relation into sections over `V' ⊓ piece z`
168	  have hyW₀ : y ∈ V' ⊓ D.piece z := ⟨hyV', hy⟩
169	  have hprod : ((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ (V' ⊓ D.piece z) y hyW₀).hom
170	      ((relCurve C R).resHom inf_le_left t
171	        * (relCurve C R).resHom inf_le_right (D.eqn z)) = 0 := by
172	    rw [map_mul]
173	    rw [show ((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ (V' ⊓ D.piece z) y hyW₀).hom
174	        ((relCurve C R).resHom inf_le_left t)
175	        = ((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ V' y hyV').hom t from
176	      TopCat.Presheaf.germ_res_apply _ _ _ _ _]
177	    rw [show ((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ (V' ⊓ D.piece z) y hyW₀).hom
178	        ((relCurve C R).resHom inf_le_right (D.eqn z))
179	        = ((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ (D.piece z) y hy).hom (D.eqn z) from
180	      TopCat.Presheaf.germ_res_apply _ _ _ _ _]
181	    rw [ht]
182	    exact hτ
183	  -- the product vanishes on a neighbourhood of `y`
184	  obtain ⟨W₁, hyW₁, i₁, i₂, heq⟩ := (relCurve C R).presheaf.germ_eq y hyW₀ hyW₀
185	    ((relCurve C R).resHom inf_le_left t
186	      * (relCurve C R).resHom inf_le_right (D.eqn z)) 0
187	    (by rw [hprod, map_zero])
188	  rw [map_zero] at heq
189	  -- shrink to a basic sub-open of the piece
190	  obtain ⟨f, hfle, hyf⟩ := (D.isAffineOpen_piece z).exists_basicOpen_le
191	    (⟨y, hyW₁⟩ : W₁) hy
192	  have hres := congrArg ((relCurve C R).resHom hfle) heq
193	  rw [map_zero, show i₁ = homOfLE i₁.le from Subsingleton.elim _ _] at hres
194	  rw [show (relCurve C R).resHom hfle
195	      (((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE i₁.le).op).hom
196	        ((relCurve C R).resHom inf_le_left t
197	          * (relCurve C R).resHom inf_le_right (D.eqn z)))
198	      = (relCurve C R).resHom (hfle.trans i₁.le)
199	        ((relCurve C R).resHom inf_le_left t
200	          * (relCurve C R).resHom inf_le_right (D.eqn z)) from
201	    Scheme.resHom_resHom _ _ _] at hres
202	  rw [map_mul, Scheme.resHom_resHom, Scheme.resHom_resHom] at hres
203	  -- regularity on the basic sub-open kills the cofactor
204	  have ht0 : (relCurve C R).resHom ((hfle.trans i₁.le).trans inf_le_left) t = 0 :=
205	    (mul_right_mem_nonZeroDivisors_eq_zero_iff
206	      (D.res_eqn_mem_nonZeroDivisors hD z f)).mp hres
207	  -- the original stalk element was zero
208	  rw [← ht, show ((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ V' y hyV').hom t
209	      = ((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ ((relCurve C R).basicOpen f) y hyf).hom
210	        ((relCurve C R).resHom ((hfle.trans i₁.le).trans inf_le_left) t) from
211	    (TopCat.Presheaf.germ_res_apply _ _ _ _ _).symm, ht0, map_zero]
212	
213	/-! ### The overlap ratio units -/
214	
215	/-- **The ratio law of the seed's equations** (the `LocalEquations.ratio_isUnit` clause):
216	on the overlap of two pieces the equations differ by a unit.  Each equation divides the
217	other generator's component (`dvd` crosswise), the side matching transports components
218	across the charts, and mutual divisibility against a regular section is a unit ratio. -/
219	theorem exists_ratioUnit [IsNoetherianRing R] (hD : D.IsGenerator) (z z' : relCurve C R) :
220	    ∃ u : Γ(relCurve C R, D.piece z ⊓ D.piece z')ˣ,
221	      (relCurve C R).resHom inf_le_left (D.eqn z)
222	        = (u : Γ(relCurve C R, D.piece z ⊓ D.piece z'))
223	          * (relCurve C R).resHom inf_le_right (D.eqn z') := by
224	  have hWle : D.piece z ⊓ D.piece z'
225	      ≤ relPinnedChart C R π (D.side z) ⊓ relPinnedChart C R π (D.side z') :=
226	    inf_le_inf (D.piece_le z) (D.piece_le z')
227	  -- crosswise divisibility on the pieces
228	  obtain ⟨c₁, hc₁⟩ := Ideal.mem_span_singleton.mp (hD.dvd z (D.sec_mem z'))
229	  obtain ⟨c₂, hc₂⟩ := Ideal.mem_span_singleton.mp (hD.dvd z' (D.sec_mem z))
230	  -- the restricted equations are the side components of the generators on the overlap
231	  have hF1 : (relCurve C R).resHom
232	        (inf_le_left : D.piece z ⊓ D.piece z' ≤ D.piece z) (D.eqn z)
233	      = relThetaResSide a (D.side z) (hWle.trans inf_le_left) (D.sec z) :=
234	    resHom_relThetaResSide a (D.side z) (D.piece_le z) inf_le_left (D.sec z)
235	  have hF2 : (relCurve C R).resHom
236	        (inf_le_right : D.piece z ⊓ D.piece z' ≤ D.piece z') (D.eqn z')
237	      = relThetaResSide a (D.side z') (hWle.trans inf_le_right) (D.sec z') :=
238	    resHom_relThetaResSide a (D.side z') (D.piece_le z') inf_le_right (D.sec z')
239	  -- the crosswise divisibilities, restricted to the overlap
240	  have hF3 : relThetaResSide a (D.side z) (hWle.trans inf_le_left) (D.sec z')
241	      = (relCurve C R).resHom (inf_le_left : D.piece z ⊓ D.piece z' ≤ D.piece z) (D.eqn z)
242	        * (relCurve C R).resHom inf_le_left c₁ := by
243	    have h := congrArg ((relCurve C R).resHom
244	      (inf_le_left : D.piece z ⊓ D.piece z' ≤ D.piece z)) hc₁
245	    rw [map_mul] at h
246	    exact (resHom_relThetaResSide a (D.side z) (D.piece_le z)
247	      inf_le_left (D.sec z')).symm.trans h
248	  have hF4 : relThetaResSide a (D.side z') (hWle.trans inf_le_right) (D.sec z)
249	      = (relCurve C R).resHom
250	          (inf_le_right : D.piece z ⊓ D.piece z' ≤ D.piece z') (D.eqn z')
251	        * (relCurve C R).resHom inf_le_right c₂ := by
252	    have h := congrArg ((relCurve C R).resHom
253	      (inf_le_right : D.piece z ⊓ D.piece z' ≤ D.piece z')) hc₂
254	    rw [map_mul] at h
255	    exact (resHom_relThetaResSide a (D.side z') (D.piece_le z')
256	      inf_le_right (D.sec z)).symm.trans h
257	  -- the side matching for both generators
258	  have hM : ∀ ψ : relThetaSections C R π a,
259	      relThetaResSide a (D.side z) (hWle.trans inf_le_left) ψ
260	        = (relThetaSideUnit a (D.side z) (D.side z') hWle :
261	              Γ(relCurve C R, D.piece z ⊓ D.piece z'))
262	          * relThetaResSide a (D.side z') (hWle.trans inf_le_right) ψ :=

8	/-!
9	# CHART-U(b) — datum-level openness of the chart-membership (witness) locus
10	(`informal/w4-datb-worksheet.md` §1.6, `informal/w4-datc-worksheet.md` §3.3)
11	
12	The affine-level heart of the shared CHART-U(b) brick, stated directly on a pinned
13	basic-open cocycle datum in the **witness form** the `chartLocus` predicate uses.
14	
15	For a datum `D` over an affine base `B`, the locus of primes `q` of `B` at which the
16	fibre class of `D` at `κ(q)` admits an effective witness divisor with vanishing `H¹`
17	is Zariski-open in `Spec B`.  This is the single sanctioned openness mechanism of the
18	campaign (`datumRigidEngine_isOpen_vanishing`, Noetherian-free — dat-d §3.5) read
19	through the two-way datum dictionary of C1
20	(`BasicOpenCocycleDatum.subsingleton_h1_tensor_iff_exists_witness`,
21	`informal/w4-datc-worksheet.md` GAP-6): the engine open is the complex-form fibre
22	condition `Subsingleton (H¹(pair D) ⊗[B] κ(q))`, and the dictionary rewrites it,
23	pointwise and class-intrinsically, as the effective-witness/h¹-vanishing condition.
24	
25	Role in the CHART-U(b) chain (the two unlanded links of §5 risk 1):
26	
27	* **the shifted-datum constructor (link 1):** over the étale carrier `B` the plus
28	  class collapses to an honest Čech class; twisted by the theta layer and DAT-C's
29	  GAP-1 inverse datum into the `λθᵐ(Σ-shift)⁻¹` class, then extracted
30	  (`BasicOpenCocycleDatum.exists_cechPicClass_eq`) to a datum `D`.  The output of
31	  that link is exactly a `BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π` — the input of the theorem
32	  below, whose witness set is then the `chartLocus`-over-`B`.
33	* **the étale-image openness transport (link 2):** the locus over the test base `A`
34	  is the image, under the (open, surjective) étale carrier map `Spec B → Spec A`, of
35	  the open locus this theorem produces — carried to `A` by mathlib's
36	  `IsOpenMap.isQuotientMap`/`IsQuotientMap.isOpen_preimage` once the fibre-field
37	  invariance identifies the preimage.
38	
39	The theorem is class-intrinsic (any datum in the class has the same witness set, by
40	(V1a)), so a change of extracted representative is free.
41	-/

69	/-- **CHART-U(b), the datum-level witness-locus openness** (`w4-datc` §3.3 step (3)):
70	for a pinned basic-open cocycle datum `D` over the affine base `B`, the locus of primes

78	pointwise the engine's complex-form condition `Subsingleton (H¹(pair D) ⊗[B] κ(q))`
79	is exactly the existence of such a witness. -/
80	theorem BasicOpenCocycleDatum.isOpen_setOf_exists_witness_h1_vanishing
81	    (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π) (hπ : π ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom) :

83	      ∃ W : ((C ⊗ overSpec k q.asIdeal.ResidueField).left).CurveDivisor,

85	            = Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C B q.asIdeal.ResidueField) D.cechPicClass
86	          ∧ Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule
87	              ((C ⊗ overSpec k q.asIdeal.ResidueField).left.divisorSheaf
88	                q.asIdeal.ResidueField W) 1)} := by
89	  have hset : {q : PrimeSpectrum B |
90	      ∃ W : ((C ⊗ overSpec k q.asIdeal.ResidueField).left).CurveDivisor,
91	        Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass q.asIdeal.ResidueField W
92	            = Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C B q.asIdeal.ResidueField) D.cechPicClass
93	          ∧ Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule
94	              ((C ⊗ overSpec k q.asIdeal.ResidueField).left.divisorSheaf
95	                q.asIdeal.ResidueField W) 1)}
96	      = {p : PrimeSpectrum B |
97	          Subsingleton ((datumPair D).H1 ⊗[B] p.asIdeal.ResidueField)} := by
98	    refine Set.ext fun q => ?_
99	    exact (D.subsingleton_h1_tensor_iff_exists_witness q.asIdeal.ResidueField).symm
100	  rw [hset]

103	/-! ## The openness transport (CHART-U(b) link 2, topological half)
104	
105	The engine produces the open witness locus over the étale carrier `Spec B` (or, on the
106	away pieces, over `Spec (Localization.Away f)`).  CHART-U(b)'s transport (ii)
107	(`w4-datb` §1.6, "the Kleiman tex 2204-2244 step, now one `IsOpenMap` application")
108	carries it down to the test base `Spec A` along the étale carrier map, which is open
109	and surjective.  The pure-topology core of that step is below; the remaining
110	mathematical content of link 2 is the *fibre-field invariance* that identifies the
111	preimage of the base locus with the carrier locus (`κ(q)/κ(p)` a separable extension;
112	`isH1VanishingAt_comap_away_iff` is the landed avatar for the away case). -/
113	
114	/-- **Openness descends along an open continuous surjection**: if `f` is continuous,
115	open, and surjective and `f ⁻¹' V` is open, then `V` is open — because
116	`V = f '' (f ⁻¹' V)` (surjectivity) and `f` carries opens to opens.  This is the
117	topological core of CHART-U(b)'s transport (ii). -/
118	theorem isOpen_of_isOpen_preimage_of_isOpenMap_surjective
119	    {X Y : Type*} [TopologicalSpace X] [TopologicalSpace Y] {f : X → Y}
120	    (hcont : Continuous f) (hopen : IsOpenMap f) (hsurj : Function.Surjective f)
121	    {V : Set Y} (hV : IsOpen (f ⁻¹' V)) : IsOpen V :=
122	  ((hopen.isQuotientMap hcont hsurj).isOpen_preimage).mp hV
123	
124	/-- **The `Spec`-level openness transport of CHART-U(b)** (transport (ii), topological
125	half): for a ring map `f : R →+* S` whose induced `Spec S → Spec R` is open and
126	surjective (e.g. an étale carrier map), a locus of `Spec R` whose preimage in `Spec S`
127	is open is itself open.  The engine's open witness locus lives on the carrier `Spec S`;
128	this pushes it to the test base `Spec R`. -/
129	theorem isOpen_of_isOpen_comap_preimage {R S : Type u} [CommRing R] [CommRing S]
130	    (f : R →+* S) (hopen : IsOpenMap (PrimeSpectrum.comap f))
131	    (hsurj : Function.Surjective (PrimeSpectrum.comap f))
132	    {V : Set (PrimeSpectrum R)} (hV : IsOpen (PrimeSpectrum.comap f ⁻¹' V)) :
133	    IsOpen V :=
134	  isOpen_of_isOpen_preimage_of_isOpenMap_surjective
135	    (PrimeSpectrum.continuous_comap f) hopen hsurj hV
136	
137	end AlgebraicGeometry

1	/-

4	Authors: The AlgebraicJacobian Contributors
5	-/
6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivisorFamilyTheta
7	import AlgebraicJacobian.Cohomology.RigidEngine4Relative
8	
9	/-!
10	# DDR-3 infrastructure — flatness of chart sections and side-uniform theta components
11	
12	The substrate of the relative local-generator construction
13	(`AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivSchemeFamily`, `informal/spec-dd-r.md` §3 item 3):
14	
15	* `AlgebraicGeometry.flat_sections_basicOpen` — flatness of a section ring over the base
16	  descends to basic opens (`IsAffineOpen.isLocalization_basicOpen` + localization
17	  flatness + `Module.Flat.trans`);
18	* `AlgebraicGeometry.sections_mem_nonZeroDivisors_of_forall_germ`,
19	  `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_unit_mul_of_mutual_dvd` — germwise regularity gives
20	  section-level regularity, and mutual divisibility against a regular section is a unit
21	  ratio (the ratio-unit engine);
22	* `AlgebraicGeometry.relPinnedChart`, `flat_sections_relPinnedChart` — the two pinned
23	  charts of the relative curve indexed by a `Bool` side, with the free-base-change
24	  flatness `Γ(C_R, Vᵢᴿ) = R ⊗[k] Γ(C, Vᵢ)` (`free_relSections`);
25	* `AlgebraicGeometry.relThetaResSide`, `relThetaSideUnit`, `relThetaResSide_matching` —
26	  the side-uniform chart components of a global theta section (`relThetaResFst/Snd`
27	  packaged over the side index) and their matching through the theta cocycle.
28	-/
29	
30	set_option autoImplicit false
31	set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false
32	
33	universe u
34	
35	open CategoryTheory TopologicalSpace Opposite
36	open scoped TensorProduct
37	
38	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
39	
40	attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra
41	
42	/-! ## The flatness ladder: section rings of basic opens are flat over the test ring -/
43	
44	section BasicOpenFlat
45	
46	variable (K : Type u) [CommRing K] {X : Scheme.{u}} [X.Over (Spec (.of K))]
47	
48	/-- **Flatness descends to basic opens**: for an affine open `V` with `Γ(X, V)` flat over
49	the base ring `K`, the section ring of any basic open `D(f) ⊆ V` is flat over `K` —
50	`Γ(X, D(f))` is a localization of `Γ(X, V)` (`IsAffineOpen.isLocalization_basicOpen`),
51	localizations are flat, and flatness composes along the scalar tower
52	`K → Γ(X, V) → Γ(X, D(f))`. -/
53	theorem flat_sections_basicOpen {V : X.Opens} (hV : IsAffineOpen V)
54	    (hflat : Module.Flat K Γ(X, V)) (f : Γ(X, V)) :
55	    Module.Flat K Γ(X, X.basicOpen f) := by
56	  haveI := hflat
57	  haveI := hV.isLocalization_basicOpen f
58	  haveI : Module.Flat Γ(X, V) Γ(X, X.basicOpen f) :=
59	    IsLocalization.flat _ (Submonoid.powers f)
60	  haveI : IsScalarTower K Γ(X, V) Γ(X, X.basicOpen f) :=
61	    IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_eq fun r =>
62	      (X.overAlgebraMap_apply_res K (homOfLE (X.basicOpen_le f)).op r).symm
63	  exact Module.Flat.trans K Γ(X, V) Γ(X, X.basicOpen f)
64	
65	end BasicOpenFlat
66	
67	/-! ## Section-level and unit-ratio consequences of germwise regularity -/
68	
69	section GermRegular
70	
71	variable {X : Scheme.{u}}
72	
73	/-- A section all of whose germs are nonzerodivisors is a nonzerodivisor
74	(sections of a sheaf inject into the product of their germs). -/
75	theorem sections_mem_nonZeroDivisors_of_forall_germ {W : X.Opens} {s : Γ(X, W)}
76	    (hreg : ∀ (y : X) (hy : y ∈ W),
77	      (X.presheaf.germ W y hy).hom s ∈ nonZeroDivisors (X.presheaf.stalk y)) :
78	    s ∈ nonZeroDivisors Γ(X, W) := by
79	  rw [mem_nonZeroDivisors_iff_right]
80	  intro t ht
81	  apply TopCat.Presheaf.section_ext X.sheaf W t 0
82	  intro y hy
83	  rw [map_zero]
84	  have key : (X.presheaf.germ W y hy).hom t * (X.presheaf.germ W y hy).hom s = 0 := by
85	    rw [← map_mul, ht, map_zero]
86	  exact (mul_right_mem_nonZeroDivisors_eq_zero_iff (hreg y hy)).mp key
87	
88	/-- **Mutual divisibility against a germwise-regular section is a unit ratio**: if
89	`s = c₁ · t` and `t = c₂ · s` with every germ of `s` a nonzerodivisor, then `c₁` is a
90	unit, so `s = u · t` — the ratio-unit engine of the local-generator construction. -/
91	theorem exists_unit_mul_of_mutual_dvd {W : X.Opens} {s t c₁ c₂ : Γ(X, W)}
92	    (hreg : ∀ (y : X) (hy : y ∈ W),
93	      (X.presheaf.germ W y hy).hom s ∈ nonZeroDivisors (X.presheaf.stalk y))
94	    (h₁ : s = c₁ * t) (h₂ : t = c₂ * s) :
95	    ∃ u : Γ(X, W)ˣ, s = (u : Γ(X, W)) * t := by
96	  have hzero : (1 - c₁ * c₂) * s = 0 := by
97	    rw [sub_mul, one_mul, mul_assoc, ← h₂, ← h₁, sub_self]
98	  have hone : c₁ * c₂ = 1 := by
99	    have h := (mul_right_mem_nonZeroDivisors_eq_zero_iff
100	      (sections_mem_nonZeroDivisors_of_forall_germ hreg)).mp hzero
101	    rwa [sub_eq_zero, eq_comm] at h
102	  exact ⟨Units.mkOfMulEqOne c₁ c₂ hone, h₁⟩
103	
104	end GermRegular
105	
106	/-! ## The pinned chart of a side and the side-uniform theta components -/
107	
108	section Sides
109	
110	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
111	variable (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [Algebra k R]
112	variable (π : C.left ⟶ P1 k) [IsFinite π]
113	
114	/-- The pinned chart of a side: `V₀ᴿ` for `false`, `V₁ᴿ` for `true`. -/
115	noncomputable def relPinnedChart : Bool → (relCurve C R).Opens
116	  | false => (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀
117	  | true => (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁
118	
119	@[simp]
120	lemma relPinnedChart_false :
121	    relPinnedChart C R π false = (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀ := rfl
122	
123	@[simp]
124	lemma relPinnedChart_true :
125	    relPinnedChart C R π true = (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁ := rfl
126	
127	/-- Both pinned charts are affine. -/
128	lemma isAffineOpen_relPinnedChart (b : Bool) : IsAffineOpen (relPinnedChart C R π b) := by
129	  cases b
130	  · exact relCover_isAffineOpen₀ C R (fiberTwoCover π)
131	  · exact relCover_isAffineOpen₁ C R (fiberTwoCover π)
132	
133	/-- **Flatness of the pinned chart sections over the test ring**: `Γ(C_R, Vᵢᴿ)` is the
134	free base change `R ⊗[k] Γ(C, Vᵢ)` (`free_relSections`), hence flat. -/
135	theorem flat_sections_relPinnedChart (b : Bool) :
136	    Module.Flat R Γ(relCurve C R, relPinnedChart C R π b) := by
137	  cases b
138	  · haveI : Module.Free R Γ(relCurve C R, relPinnedChart C R π false) :=
139	      free_relSections C R (fiberChart₀ π)
140	        (isAffineOpen_preimage_chartOpen π 0).isCompact
141	        (isAffineOpen_preimage_chartOpen π 0).isQuasiSeparated
142	    exact Module.Flat.of_free
143	  · haveI : Module.Free R Γ(relCurve C R, relPinnedChart C R π true) :=
144	      free_relSections C R (fiberChart₁ π)
145	        (isAffineOpen_preimage_chartOpen π 1).isCompact
146	        (isAffineOpen_preimage_chartOpen π 1).isQuasiSeparated
147	    exact Module.Flat.of_free
148	
149	variable {C R π}
150	variable (a : ℕ)
151	
152	/-- **The side-uniform chart component of a global theta section**, restricted into an
153	open below the pinned chart of the side: `relThetaResFst` on side `false`,
154	`relThetaResSnd` on side `true`. -/
155	noncomputable def relThetaResSide :
156	    ∀ (b : Bool) {W : (relCurve C R).Opens}, W ≤ relPinnedChart C R π b →
157	      (relThetaSections C R π a →ₗ[R] Γ(relCurve C R, W))
158	  | false, _, hW => relThetaResFst a (le_inf le_top hW)
159	  | true, _, hW => relThetaResSnd a (le_inf le_top hW)
160	
161	@[simp]
162	lemma relThetaResSide_false {W : (relCurve C R).Opens}
163	    (hW : W ≤ relPinnedChart C R π false) (x : relThetaSections C R π a) :
164	    relThetaResSide a false hW x = (relCurve C R).resHom (le_inf le_top hW) x.val.1 := rfl
165	
166	@[simp]
167	lemma relThetaResSide_true {W : (relCurve C R).Opens}
168	    (hW : W ≤ relPinnedChart C R π true) (x : relThetaSections C R π a) :
169	    relThetaResSide a true hW x = (relCurve C R).resHom (le_inf le_top hW) x.val.2 := rfl
170	
171	/-- The side components commute with restriction. -/
172	lemma resHom_relThetaResSide (b : Bool) {W W' : (relCurve C R).Opens}
173	    (hW : W ≤ relPinnedChart C R π b) (h' : W' ≤ W) (x : relThetaSections C R π a) :
174	    (relCurve C R).resHom h' (relThetaResSide a b hW x)
175	      = relThetaResSide a b (h'.trans hW) x := by
176	  cases b <;> exact Scheme.resHom_resHom _ _ _
177	
178	/-- **The matching unit of an ordered pair of sides** on an open below both pinned
179	charts: `1` on equal sides, the theta cocycle (resp. its inverse) across the charts. -/
180	noncomputable def relThetaSideUnit :
181	    ∀ (b b' : Bool) {W : (relCurve C R).Opens},
182	      W ≤ relPinnedChart C R π b ⊓ relPinnedChart C R π b' → Γ(relCurve C R, W)ˣ
183	  | false, false, _, _ => 1
184	  | false, true, _, hW => (relCurve C R).unitsRestrict hW (relThetaCocycle C R π a)
185	  | true, false, _, hW =>
186	      ((relCurve C R).unitsRestrict
187	        (le_inf (hW.trans inf_le_right) (hW.trans inf_le_left))
188	        (relThetaCocycle C R π a))⁻¹
189	  | true, true, _, _ => 1
190	
191	/-- **The side matching law**: on an open below both pinned charts, the two side
192	components of a global theta section differ by the side matching unit
193	(`relThetaSections_matching` in side-uniform form). -/
194	lemma relThetaResSide_matching (b b' : Bool) {W : (relCurve C R).Opens}
195	    (hW : W ≤ relPinnedChart C R π b ⊓ relPinnedChart C R π b')
196	    (x : relThetaSections C R π a) :
197	    relThetaResSide a b (hW.trans inf_le_left) x
198	      = (relThetaSideUnit a b b' hW : Γ(relCurve C R, W))
199	        * relThetaResSide a b' (hW.trans inf_le_right) x := by
200	  cases b <;> cases b'
201	  · rw [show relThetaSideUnit a false false hW = 1 from rfl, Units.val_one, one_mul]
202	  · exact relThetaSections_matching a x hW
203	  · have key := relThetaSections_matching a x
204	      (le_inf (hW.trans inf_le_right) (hW.trans inf_le_left))
205	    change relThetaResSide a true (hW.trans inf_le_left) x
206	        = ↑((relCurve C R).unitsRestrict
207	            (le_inf (hW.trans inf_le_right) (hW.trans inf_le_left))
208	            (relThetaCocycle C R π a))⁻¹
209	          * relThetaResSide a false (hW.trans inf_le_right) x
210	    rw [Units.eq_inv_mul_iff_mul_eq]
211	    exact key.symm
212	  · rw [show relThetaSideUnit a true true hW = 1 from rfl, Units.val_one, one_mul]
213	
214	end Sides
215	
216	end AlgebraicGeometry

338	two restrictions generate the same ideal (the equations differ by units on overlaps

341	noncomputable abbrev ovlIdeal (i j : A.index) :
342	    Ideal Γ(relCurve C R, A.pieces i ⊓ A.pieces j) :=
343	  Ideal.span
344	    {relResAlgHom C R (inf_le_left : A.pieces i ⊓ A.pieces j ≤ A.pieces i) (A.eqn i),
345	     relResAlgHom C R (inf_le_right : A.pieces i ⊓ A.pieces j ≤ A.pieces j) (A.eqn j)}

347	/-- The overlap colength module `Γ(D(h_i) ⊓ D(h_j)) ⧸ (f_i, f_j)`. -/

349	  Γ(relCurve C R, A.pieces i ⊓ A.pieces j) ⧸ A.ovlIdeal i j

354	  Ideal.Quotient.liftₐ (Ideal.span {A.eqn i})
355	    ((Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ R (A.ovlIdeal i j)).comp (relResAlgHom C R inf_le_left))

363	          ∈ A.ovlIdeal i j :=

402	verbatim); the equalizer description is `mem_gluedSubmodule_iff`. -/

446	
447	variable (n : ℕ)

450	(D1) pair `(d, c)`): a local-equation system with a certified finite chart
451	adaptation. -/
452	structure CertifiedDivisorFamily [IsAffineHom π] : Type u where
453	  /-- The local-equation system on the relative curve. -/
454	  eqns : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations
455	  /-- The finite chart adaptation refining it. -/
456	  adaptation : DivisorAdaptation C R π eqns
457	  /-- The colength certificate of degree `n`. -/
458	  certified : adaptation.IsCertified n
459

461	systems cut the same divisor (`Scheme.LocalEquations.DivEq`); the adaptation and
462	certificate are per-representative data and do not enter the relation. -/
463	def divFamSetoid [IsAffineHom π] : Setoid (CertifiedDivisorFamily C R π n) where
464	  r F G := Scheme.LocalEquations.DivEq F.eqns G.eqns
465	  iseqv :=

467	     fun h => h.symm, fun h h' => h.trans h'⟩

469	/-- **The divisor-functor value on the affine test `R`** (worksheet §1.1): certified
470	divisor families of degree `n` up to divisor equality. A `Type u` quotient — the
471	carrier the affine-opens-limit vehicle ranges over. -/
472	def DivFam [IsAffineHom π] : Type u := Quotient (divFamSetoid C R π n)

474	namespace DivFam

476	variable {C R π n} [IsAffineHom π]
477	
478	/-- The class of a certified family. -/
479	def mk (F : CertifiedDivisorFamily C R π n) : DivFam C R π n :=
480	  Quotient.mk (divFamSetoid C R π n) F
481	
482	lemma mk_eq_mk_iff {F G : CertifiedDivisorFamily C R π n} :
483	    mk F = mk G ↔ Scheme.LocalEquations.DivEq F.eqns G.eqns :=
484	  Quotient.eq (r := divFamSetoid C R π n)
485	
486	/-- **The Picard class of a divisor family** `𝒪(D)`: well defined on the quotient by
487	the class laws (`picClass_eq_of_divEq`). This is the Abel hook DAT-C consumes. -/
488	noncomputable def picClass (F : DivFam C R π n) : (relCurve C R).CechPic :=
489	  Quotient.lift (fun F : CertifiedDivisorFamily C R π n => F.eqns.picClass)
490	    (fun _ _ h => Scheme.LocalEquations.picClass_eq_of_divEq h) F
491	
492	@[simp]
493	lemma picClass_mk (F : CertifiedDivisorFamily C R π n) :
494	    picClass (mk F) = F.eqns.picClass :=
495	  rfl
496	
497	end DivFam

9	/-!
10	# Swallow or miss: the shape of an adaptation that can be certified
11	
12	`DivSchemeCertZarChartTrace.lean` shows that the assembler's per-piece no-leak clause
13	*forces* the chart traces `supportLocus ∩ V_b` to be closed.  This file gives the matching
14	sufficient condition, and it is deliberately crude:
15	
16	> if every piece either **swallows** the support (`supportLocus ⊆ pieces j`) or **misses**
17	> it (`Disjoint supportLocus (pieces j)`), then no-leak holds at every piece.
18	
19	For a swallowing piece the trace is the whole support, which is closed by construction
20	(`isClosed_supportLocus`); for a missing piece the trace is empty.  Neither case needs a
21	fibre, a tube, or an idempotent.
22	
23	The crudeness is not a defect, because the necessity lemma pins down exactly how much
24	freedom is left.  Both pinned charts are covered by their pieces, so
25	
26	* if some chart-`b` piece meets the support it must swallow it, whence `supportLocus ⊆ V_b`;
27	* otherwise every chart-`b` piece misses the support, whence `supportLocus ∩ V_b = ∅`.
28	
29	Since `V₀ ⊔ V₁` is the whole relative curve, a nonempty support therefore lies in
30	`V₀ ⊓ V₁` — the divisor must avoid **both** vertical fibres `pi⁻¹(0)` and `pi⁻¹(∞)` — or be
31	confined to one of them.  That is the honest chart-design hypothesis of the lane, and it is
32	where the DD-R atlas has to do its work; it is not something a support tube, a packet
33	idempotent, or a shrink of the base can manufacture.
34	
35	A missing piece contributes nothing at all: its equation is a unit, so its colength module
36	vanishes (`subsingleton_colength_of_disjoint_supportLocus`) and clauses (c1) hold there for
37	free — no fibrewise regularity input.  So the certificate of a swallow-or-miss adaptation is
38	carried entirely by the swallowing pieces, at most one per chart.
39	
40	## Main declarations
41	
42	* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivisorAdaptation.subsingleton_colength_of_disjoint_supportLocus` — a
43	  piece missing the support has a vanishing colength.
44	* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivisorAdaptation.supportLeak_eq_empty_of_subset_or_disjoint` — swallow
45	  or miss gives no-leak at that piece.
46	* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivisorAdaptation.forall_noLeak_of_forall_subset_or_disjoint` — the
47	  assembler-shaped `hnoLeak`, with no fibre analysis.
48	* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivisorAdaptation.forall_finite_colength_of_forall_subset_or_disjoint` —
49	  clause (c1)-finite at every piece.
50	* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivisorAdaptation.subset_chart₀_or_disjoint_chart₀` /
51	  `…_chart₁_…` — the design constraint the shape imposes on the divisor.
52	-/

75	/-! ## A piece missing the support contributes nothing -/
76	
77	/-- **A piece that misses the support has a vanishing colength.** Its equation has a unit
78	germ at every point of the piece (`isUnit_germ_eqn_iff` read through the unit locus), hence
79	is a unit (`RingedSpace.isUnit_of_isUnit_germ`), hence spans the unit ideal.
80	
81	This is the colength companion of `subsingleton_ovlColength_of_disjoint_supportLocus`: on
82	such a piece the certificate's clauses (c1) are free, with no fibrewise regularity input. -/
83	lemma subsingleton_colength_of_disjoint_supportLocus (j : A.index)
84	    (hdisj : ∀ z : relCurve C R, z ∈ A.pieces j → z ∉ d.supportLocus) :
85	    Subsingleton (A.colength j) := by
86	  have hunit : IsUnit (A.eqn j) := by
87	    apply (relCurve C R).toRingedSpace.isUnit_of_isUnit_germ
88	    intro z hz
89	    have hU : z ∈ d.unitLocus := not_not.mp (hdisj z hz)
90	    exact (A.isUnit_germ_eqn_iff j hz).mpr
91	      ((d.mem_unitLocus_iff_isUnit_germ (d.cover.mem_opens z)).mp hU)
92	  exact Ideal.Quotient.subsingleton_iff.mpr
93	    (Ideal.eq_top_of_isUnit_mem _ (Ideal.subset_span rfl) hunit)
94	
95	/-! ## Swallow or miss gives no-leak -/
96	
97	/-- **Swallow or miss gives no-leak at that piece.** If the piece contains the whole support
98	its trace is the support, closed by `isClosed_supportLocus`; if the piece misses the support
99	its trace is empty.  In neither case is a fibre, a tube or an idempotent involved. -/
100	theorem supportLeak_eq_empty_of_subset_or_disjoint (j : A.index)
101	    (h : d.supportLocus ⊆ (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R))
102	      ∨ Disjoint d.supportLocus (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R))) :
103	    d.supportLeak (A.pieces j) = ∅ := by
104	  refine (d.isClosed_supportLocus_inter_iff_supportLeak_eq_empty (A.pieces j)).mp ?_
105	  rcases h with hsub | hdisj
106	  · rw [Set.inter_eq_left.mpr hsub]
107	    exact d.isClosed_supportLocus
108	  · rw [Set.disjoint_iff_inter_eq_empty.mp hdisj]
109	    exact isClosed_empty
110	
111	/-- **The assembler-shaped `hnoLeak` from swallow-or-miss.** This is the hypothesis of
112	`isCertified_of_noLeak_kernel_spanning` /
113	`isCertified_of_noLeak_of_forall_liftQ_injective` /
114	`divisorAdaptation_isCertified_of_noLeak_liftQ_degree`, produced with no fibre analysis. -/
115	theorem forall_noLeak_of_forall_subset_or_disjoint
116	    (h : ∀ j : A.index, d.supportLocus ⊆ (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R))
117	      ∨ Disjoint d.supportLocus (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R))) :
118	    ∀ (j : A.index) (s : Spec (.of R)),
119	      ((relCurve C R) ↘ Spec (.of R)).base ⁻¹' {s}
120	          ∩ closure (d.supportLocus ∩ (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R))) ⊆
121	        (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R)) := by
122	  intro j s x hx
123	  have hleak := A.supportLeak_eq_empty_of_subset_or_disjoint j (h j)
124	  by_contra hxU
125	  exact Set.eq_empty_iff_forall_notMem.mp hleak x ⟨hx.2, hxU⟩

143	/-! ## What the shape forces on the divisor
144	
145	The necessity direction of `DivSchemeCertZarChartTrace.lean` is sharpened here: because the
146	chart-`b` pieces cover `V_b`, a swallow-or-miss adaptation exists only for a divisor that is
147	either inside a pinned chart or disjoint from it.  Combined with `V₀ ⊔ V₁ = ⊤` this says a
148	nonempty support lies in `V₀ ⊓ V₁`, or is confined to one vertical fibre of `pi`.
149	
150	This is the statement the DD-R atlas owes: **the chart's divisors avoid `pi⁻¹(0)` and
151	`pi⁻¹(∞)`.**  It is a hypothesis about the chart, and it is the only remaining geometric
152	input of the (c1) side of the certificate. -/
153	
154	/-- **Chart-0 dichotomy.** A swallow-or-miss adaptation forces the support either inside the
155	pinned chart `V₀` or disjoint from it. -/
156	theorem subset_chart₀_or_disjoint_chart₀
157	    (h : ∀ j : A.index, d.supportLocus ⊆ (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R))
158	      ∨ Disjoint d.supportLocus (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R))) :
159	    d.supportLocus ⊆ ((relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀ : Set (relCurve C R))
160	      ∨ Disjoint d.supportLocus
161	        ((relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀ : Set (relCurve C R)) := by
162	  by_cases hmeet : ∃ j : Fin A.m₀, d.supportLocus ⊆ (A.pieces (Sum.inl j) : Set (relCurve C R))
163	  · obtain ⟨j, hj⟩ := hmeet
164	    exact Or.inl (hj.trans fun x hx => (relCurve C R).basicOpen_le (A.h₀ j) hx)
165	  · refine Or.inr (Set.disjoint_iff_inter_eq_empty.mpr ?_)
166	    rw [A.supportLocus_inter_chart₀_eq_iUnion]
167	    refine Set.iUnion_eq_empty.mpr fun j => Set.disjoint_iff_inter_eq_empty.mp ?_
168	    exact (h (Sum.inl j)).resolve_left fun hsub => hmeet ⟨j, hsub⟩
169	
170	/-- **Chart-1 dichotomy.** -/
171	theorem subset_chart₁_or_disjoint_chart₁
172	    (h : ∀ j : A.index, d.supportLocus ⊆ (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R))
173	      ∨ Disjoint d.supportLocus (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R))) :
174	    d.supportLocus ⊆ ((relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁ : Set (relCurve C R))
175	      ∨ Disjoint d.supportLocus
176	        ((relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁ : Set (relCurve C R)) := by
177	  by_cases hmeet : ∃ j : Fin A.m₁, d.supportLocus ⊆ (A.pieces (Sum.inr j) : Set (relCurve C R))
178	  · obtain ⟨j, hj⟩ := hmeet
179	    exact Or.inl (hj.trans fun x hx => (relCurve C R).basicOpen_le (A.h₁ j) hx)
180	  · refine Or.inr (Set.disjoint_iff_inter_eq_empty.mpr ?_)
181	    rw [A.supportLocus_inter_chart₁_eq_iUnion]
182	    refine Set.iUnion_eq_empty.mpr fun j => Set.disjoint_iff_inter_eq_empty.mp ?_
183	    exact (h (Sum.inr j)).resolve_left fun hsub => hmeet ⟨j, hsub⟩

9	/-!
10	# The chart trace is what no-leak really asks for
11	
12	The certificate assemblers consume, per piece `j`, the fibrewise no-leak clause, which is
13	emptiness of the leak locus, which is closedness of the piece trace
14	`supportLocus ∩ pieces j` (`isClosed_supportLocus_inter_iff_supportLeak_eq_empty`), which
15	is clopen-ness of that trace inside the support (`isClopen_trace_of_supportLeak_eq_empty`).
16	
17	This file records the consequence that had been missed for the whole lifetime of the lane:
18	**the per-piece clause cannot be produced piece by piece.**  A `FinCoverData` carries a
19	partition of unity on each pinned chart, so the chart-`b` pieces cover the *whole* pinned
20	chart `V_b` — hence the union of their traces is the whole chart trace
21	`supportLocus ∩ V_b`.  A finite union of closed sets is closed, so
22	
23	> no-leak at every chart-`b` piece **forces** `supportLocus ∩ V_b` to be closed in the
24	> relative curve, i.e. the chart trace to be clopen in the support.
25	
26	That is a property of the *system and the pinned charts alone*: no choice of adaptation, and
27	no shrinking of the base, can produce no-leak for a system whose chart trace is not closed.
28	It is therefore the honest gate of the lane, and it replaces the refuted `tube-fibre`
29	framing (put the support inside one piece — impossible once the support meets both charts,
30	`not_exists_unique_support_piece`) and the refuted separated framing
31	(`DivSchemeCertZarSep.lean`) with a single geometric statement about the divisor.
32	
33	Read positively, it also says where to aim: `supportLocus ∩ V₀` and `supportLocus ∩ V₁`
34	closed is not merely necessary, it is *sufficient*, because the two-piece adaptation whose
35	pieces are the pinned charts themselves realizes it (`DivSchemeCertZarChartPair.lean`).
36	
37	## Main declarations
38	
39	* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivisorAdaptation.supportLocus_inter_chart₀_eq_iUnion` /
40	  `…_chart₁_…` — the chart trace is the finite union of the chart's piece traces.
41	* `DivisorAdaptation.isClosed_supportLocus_inter_chart₀_of_forall_supportLeak_eq_empty`
42	  and its chart-1 twin — no-leak at every piece of a chart forces the chart trace closed.
43	* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivisorAdaptation.isClosed_supportLocus_inter_chart_of_forall_noLeak` —
44	  the assembler-shaped form: the `hnoLeak` hypothesis of
45	  `isCertified_of_noLeak_kernel_spanning` forces both chart traces closed.
46	* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivisorAdaptation.not_forall_noLeak_of_not_isClosed_chart₀` — the
47	  obstruction, contrapositive: a system with a non-closed chart-0 trace admits **no**
48	  adaptation satisfying the assembler's no-leak clause.
49	-/

78	    d.supportLocus ∩ ((relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀ : Set (relCurve C R))

82	    obtain ⟨j, hj⟩ := Opens.mem_iSup.mp (A.toFinCoverData.cover₀ hxV)
83	    exact Set.mem_iUnion.mpr ⟨j, hxs, hj⟩
84	  · refine Set.iUnion_subset fun j x hx => ⟨hx.1, ?_⟩
85	    exact (relCurve C R).basicOpen_le (A.h₀ j) hx.2

100	/-- **No-leak at every chart-0 piece forces the chart-0 trace closed.** The trace of the
101	whole pinned chart is the finite union of the piece traces, each of which is closed exactly
102	when nothing leaks out of it. -/

104	    (h : ∀ j : Fin A.m₀, d.supportLeak (A.pieces (Sum.inl j)) = ∅) :
105	    IsClosed (d.supportLocus
106	      ∩ ((relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀ : Set (relCurve C R))) := by
107	  rw [A.supportLocus_inter_chart₀_eq_iUnion]

113	    (h : ∀ j : Fin A.m₁, d.supportLeak (A.pieces (Sum.inr j)) = ∅) :
114	    IsClosed (d.supportLocus
115	      ∩ ((relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁ : Set (relCurve C R))) := by
116	  rw [A.supportLocus_inter_chart₁_eq_iUnion]
117	  exact isClosed_iUnion_of_finite fun j =>
118	    (d.isClosed_supportLocus_inter_iff_supportLeak_eq_empty _).mpr (h j)

121	gate of the certificate lane in its irreducible form: the hypothesis of
122	`isCertified_of_noLeak_kernel_spanning` (equivalently of

124	`divisorAdaptation_isCertified_of_noLeak_liftQ_degree`) implies a statement that mentions
125	neither the adaptation nor its pieces — only the system and the two pinned charts. -/
126	theorem isClosed_supportLocus_inter_chart_of_forall_noLeak
127	    (hnoLeak : ∀ (j : A.index) (s : Spec (.of R)),
128	      ((relCurve C R) ↘ Spec (.of R)).base ⁻¹' {s}
129	          ∩ closure (d.supportLocus ∩ (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R))) ⊆
130	        (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R))) :
131	    IsClosed (d.supportLocus
132	        ∩ ((relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀ : Set (relCurve C R)))
133	      ∧ IsClosed (d.supportLocus
134	        ∩ ((relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁ : Set (relCurve C R))) := by
135	  have hleak : ∀ j : A.index, d.supportLeak (A.pieces j) = ∅ := fun j =>
136	    d.supportLeak_eq_empty_of_forall_fibre
137	      ((relCurve C R) ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of R)) (hnoLeak j)
138	  exact ⟨A.isClosed_supportLocus_inter_chart₀_of_forall_supportLeak_eq_empty

140	    A.isClosed_supportLocus_inter_chart₁_of_forall_supportLeak_eq_empty
141	      fun j => hleak (Sum.inr j)⟩

143	/-! ## The obstruction
144	
145	The contrapositive is the statement the lane needed: for a system whose chart trace is not
146	closed there is *nothing to prove* — the assembler's hypothesis is false for every
147	adaptation, so no support-tube refinement, no idempotent packet extraction and no shrinking
148	of the base can supply it.  The tube mechanism (`exists_basicOpen_supportLeak_eq_empty`)
149	is not a counterexample: it shrinks the base, and shrinking the base shrinks the system's
150	support too, so what it proves is the chart-trace statement over the smaller base. -/

152	/-- **The obstruction.** If the chart-0 trace of the system is not closed in the relative
153	curve, then no adaptation of that system satisfies the assembler's no-leak clause. -/
154	theorem not_forall_noLeak_of_not_isClosed_chart₀
155	    (hnc : ¬ IsClosed (d.supportLocus
156	      ∩ ((relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀ : Set (relCurve C R)))) :

159	          ∩ closure (d.supportLocus ∩ (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R))) ⊆
160	        (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R)) :=
161	  fun h => hnc (A.isClosed_supportLocus_inter_chart_of_forall_noLeak h).1
162

166	      ∩ ((relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁ : Set (relCurve C R)))) :

168	      ((relCurve C R) ↘ Spec (.of R)).base ⁻¹' {s}
169	          ∩ closure (d.supportLocus ∩ (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R))) ⊆

The glued carve locus of the DAT-D design (`informal/spec-dd-r.md` §3 item 1): the
chart-wise loci `Z(♦) ⊆ Spec (R^I ⊗ R^J)` (`Picard/DivCarveLocus.lean`) assemble into a
closed subscheme of `grPair` through the mathlib ideal-sheaf machinery — `carveIdealSheaf`
is the kernel ideal sheaf of the disjoint family of chart loci (the largest ideal sheaf
vanishing on all of them, `⨅ over the pair atlas`), and `DivScheme` is its subscheme.

* `AlgebraicGeometry.carveIdealSheaf`: the ideal sheaf `I_♦` on `grPair`.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.carveScheme`, `carveSchemeι`, `carveSchemeOver`: the generic glued
  locus, its closed immersion (mathlib's `IdealSheafData.subschemeι` instance), and its
  `Over (Spec k)` form.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.carveScheme_exists_factor_of_le_ker` and
  `carveIdealSheaf_le_ker_of_factors`: the factoring criterion at chart tests — a test
  map through a pair chart killing the chart carve ideal factors (uniquely, by `Mono`)
  through `carveSchemeι`.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.carveScheme_hom_ext` (`divScheme_hom_ext`, DDR-7's tail): morphisms
  into the locus are determined by their composites with the closed immersion.
* **Campaign spellings**: `DivScheme`, `divSchemeι`, `divSchemeOver` at the DAT-D
  windows.

`KeyChart` of the DD-R roadmap) rests on the landed gluing compatibility
(`carveIdeal_le_ker_of_specMap_pairChartMap_eq`); its remaining half is the app-level
localization bookkeeping and is left to the successor lane (see the inbox memory).

open Grassmannian

variable {ι : Type u} (μ : ι → ((Fin r₁ → k) →ₗ[k] (Fin r₂ → k)))

/-- **The carve ideal sheaf `I_♦`** on the Grassmannian pair: the largest ideal sheaf
vanishing on every chart-wise carve locus — the infimum of the kernels of the chart
loci mapped into `grPair`. -/
noncomputable def carveIdealSheaf : (grPair k g r₁ g r₂).IdealSheafData :=
  ⨅ c : (glueData k g r₁).J × (glueData k g r₂).J,
    (carveLocusToGrPair k g r₁ r₂ μ c.1 c.2).ker

/-- **The glued carve locus `Z(♦)`** as a scheme: the subscheme of the carve ideal
sheaf on the Grassmannian pair. -/
noncomputable def carveScheme : Scheme :=
  (carveIdealSheaf k g r₁ r₂ μ).subscheme

/-- **The closed immersion `Z(♦) ⟶ grPair`**. -/
noncomputable def carveSchemeι : carveScheme k g r₁ r₂ μ ⟶ grPair k g r₁ g r₂ :=
  (carveIdealSheaf k g r₁ r₂ μ).subschemeι

instance isClosedImmersion_carveSchemeι :
    IsClosedImmersion (carveSchemeι k g r₁ r₂ μ) :=
  inferInstanceAs (IsClosedImmersion (carveIdealSheaf k g r₁ r₂ μ).subschemeι)

/-- The kernel of the closed immersion is the carve ideal sheaf. -/
theorem ker_carveSchemeι :
    (carveSchemeι k g r₁ r₂ μ).ker = carveIdealSheaf k g r₁ r₂ μ :=
  Scheme.IdealSheafData.ker_subschemeι _

/-- **`Z(♦)` as a test object of `Over (Spec k)`**. -/
noncomputable def carveSchemeOver : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) :=
  Over.mk (carveSchemeι k g r₁ r₂ μ ≫ grPairStructMap k g r₁ g r₂)

/-- Each chart-wise carve locus maps to the glued locus over `grPair`. -/
theorem carveIdealSheaf_le_ker_carveLocusToGrPair

    carveIdealSheaf k g r₁ r₂ μ ≤ (carveLocusToGrPair k g r₁ r₂ μ i j).ker :=

    ∃ v : Spec (CommRingCat.of S) ⟶ carveScheme k g r₁ r₂ μ,

closed immersion has the carve ideal sheaf in its kernel. -/
theorem carveIdealSheaf_le_ker_of_factors {T : Scheme.{u}} (u : T ⟶ grPair k g r₁ g r₂)

  exact Scheme.Hom.le_ker_comp _ _

11	
12	The two preceding files bracket the certificate assembler's per-piece no-leak clause:
13	`DivSchemeCertZarChartTrace.lean` shows it forces the chart traces `supportLocus ∩ V_b` to
14	be closed, and `DivSchemeCertZarSwallow.lean` shows the "swallow or miss" shape produces it.
15	This file closes the bracket, and thereby decides the lane's satisfiability question.
16	
17	The observation is that leak-freeness *plus connectedness of the divisor* already implies
18	swallow-or-miss.  For each piece the trace `supportLocus ∩ pieces j` is open in the support
19	(the piece is open) and closed in it (that is leak-freeness), so a connected support leaves
20	only the two degenerate values: the trace is empty, or it is everything.  Feeding this into
21	the chart dichotomies of `DivSchemeCertZarSwallow.lean` and `relCover_sup` gives
22	
23	> **a nonempty connected divisor whose adaptation is leak-free at every piece lies inside
24	> `V₀` or inside `V₁`.**

27	pieces, adaptations, tubes or fibres: it says the certificate interface can only ever be
28	satisfied by divisors confined to one pinned chart of `pi` — a **chart-design** condition.
29	
30	Nor can a shrink of the base repair it, because base localization does not disconnect the
31	divisor: `Spec (R[x]/(x² − t))` over `R = k[t]` is connected over every basic open of
32	`Spec R`, so no Zariski neighbourhood of `t = 0` splits the divisor into clopen packets.
33	Hence the "clopen packet extraction" programme (memory I-0209) is available exactly when the
34	divisor is already chart-confined, and the honest obligation of the lane is to make the
35	DD-R atlas produce chart-confined divisors.

42	  same for every piece at once, i.e. leak-free + connected ⟹ swallow-or-miss.
43	* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivisorAdaptation.supportLocus_subset_chart_of_isPreconnected` — **the
44	  satisfiability verdict**: a nonempty connected support with a leak-free adaptation lies

/-- **DDR-9.0 — the carve discharge** (`informal/w4-ddr9-worksheet.md` §2.0, the brick no
scoreboard carried): the ε-pair of ANY certified divisor family over ANY affine test
ring satisfies the carve `(♦)` — `carvePairArrow (windowShiftMul hπ g a) ε₁ ε₂ = 0` for
every multiplier section `a ∈ H⁰(𝒪(s·F))`.  Route: membership only.  The carve arrow
vanishes iff the multiplier maps `ε₁ = K_M(d)` into `ε₂ = K_{M+s}(d)`
(`carvePairArrow_eq_zero_iff`); membership in the windows is germ-vanishing along `d`
(`mem_divisorWindow_iff`), the multiplied window image is the componentwise product of a
fixed theta section with the original image (`relThetaWindowEquiv_sectionMul_fst/_snd`),
and the stalk ideal absorbs the extra factor by `Ideal.mul_mem_left`. -/
theorem divFamEps_carve (G : CertifiedDivisorFamily C R π g)
    (a : ↥(divisorSections k (windowS_choice π hπ g • fiberWeilDivisor π) ⊤)) :
    Grassmannian.carvePairArrow (windowShiftMul hπ g a)
      (divFamEps hπ g (DivFam.mk G)).1 (divFamEps hπ g (DivFam.mk G)).2 = 0 := by
  rw [Grassmannian.carvePairArrow_eq_zero_iff]
  intro x hx
  rw [divFamEps_mk] at hx ⊢
  exact windowShiftMul_mem_divisorWindow C π hπ g R G.eqns a hx

import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivSchemeCertUniv
import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivSchemeCertFibreRank

/-!
# Certificate assembly for an extracted theta-generator adaptation

This file specializes the generic universal-family certificate assembler to the
adaptation extracted from a theta-generator seed.  No-leak supplies finite chart and
overlap colengths, seed regularity supplies their projectivity and overlap flatness,
and the degree of the pulled divisor computes the remaining fibre rank.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false
set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false

universe u

open CategoryTheory Limits TopologicalSpace Opposite

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra
attribute [local instance 10000] relCurve.instOver

namespace ThetaGeneratorSeed

variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
variable {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [Algebra k R] [IsNoetherianRing R]
variable {pi : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsFinite pi]
variable {a : Nat} {K : Submodule R (relThetaSections C R pi a)}
variable {D : ThetaGeneratorSeed C R pi a K} (hD : D.IsGenerator)

noncomputable local instance instIsIntegralRelCurveCertSeed
    (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L] : IsIntegral (relCurve C L) :=
  instIsIntegralBaseChange C L

noncomputable local instance instSmoothRelCurveCertSeed
    (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L] :
    SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (relCurve C L ↘ Spec (.of L)) :=
  instSmoothOfRelativeDimensionBaseChange C L

noncomputable local instance instQCRelCurveCertSeed
    (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L] :
    QuasiCompact (relCurve C L ↘ Spec (.of L)) :=
  instQuasiCompactBaseChange C L

local notation "A" => D.divisorAdaptation hD

/-- Assemble the certificate of an extracted theta-generator adaptation from no-leak,
relative kernel spanning, and the degree of every pulled divisor.  In particular,
overlap finiteness, overlap flatness, chart projectivity, and fibre kernel dimension
are consequences rather than separate inputs. -/
theorem divisorAdaptation_isCertified_of_noLeak_kernel_spanning_degree {n : Nat}
    (hnoLeak : forall (j : (A).index) (s : Spec (.of R)),
      ((relCurve C R) ↘ Spec (.of R)).base ⁻¹' {s}
          ∩ closure
            ((D.localEquations hD).supportLocus ∩
              ((A).pieces j : Set (relCurve C R))) ⊆
        ((A).pieces j : Set (relCurve C R)))
    (L : Submodule R (A).chartProd)
    (hle : L ≤ LinearMap.ker ((A).deltaLeft - (A).deltaRight))
    (hspan : forall p : PrimeSpectrum R,
      LinearMap.ker
          (((A).deltaLeft - (A).deltaRight).rTensor p.asIdeal.ResidueField) ≤
        LinearMap.range (L.subtype.rTensor p.asIdeal.ResidueField))
    (hdeg : forall (p : PrimeSpectrum R)
      (hproj : forall j : (A).index, Module.Projective R ((A).colength j)),
      Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg p.asIdeal.ResidueField
          (Scheme.presentationDivisor p.asIdeal.ResidueField
            (((A).pulledEquations p.asIdeal.ResidueField hproj).presentation)) =
        (n : Int)) :
    (A).IsCertified n := by
  have hfin : forall j : (A).index, Module.Finite R ((A).colength j) :=
    fun j => (A).finite_colength_of_forall_fibre_closure_subset j (hnoLeak j)
  have hproj : forall j : (A).index, Module.Projective R ((A).colength j) := by
    intro j
    letI : Module.Finite R ((A).colength j) := hfin j
    exact (A).projective_colength_of_forall_tmul_residueField j
      (D.divisorAdaptation_fibre_regular hD j)
  have hdim : forall p : PrimeSpectrum R,
      Module.finrank p.asIdeal.ResidueField
          (LinearMap.ker
            (((A).deltaLeft - (A).deltaRight).baseChange p.asIdeal.ResidueField)) = n := by
    intro p
    exact (A).finrank_ker_delta_baseChange_eq_of_pulled_degree
      (K := p.asIdeal.ResidueField) hproj (hdeg p hproj)
  exact D.divisorAdaptation_isCertified_of_noLeak_kernel_spanning
    hD hnoLeak L hle hspan hdim

end ThetaGeneratorSeed

end AlgebraicGeometry

/-!
# DDR-4 (certificate transport) — the window–engine junction `H⁰(𝒪(Θᵃ − d)) ≅ K_a(d)`

THE seam brick of the DD-R endgame (`informal/spec-dd-r.md` §3 item 4, probe verdict
GREEN): the bridge between DD-1's `gluedSubmodule`-style carriers and the rigid engine's
Čech `H⁰` of the constructed family's twisted glued sheaf.  For a divisor family `d`
with finite chart adaptation `A` on the relative curve `C_R` and a twist exponent `a`,
the global sections of the theta-ideal datum sheaf (`DivisorAdaptation.thetaIdealDatum`,
the engine-ready presentation of `𝒪(Θᵃ − d)`) are identified `R`-linearly with the
vanishing submodule `K_a(d) = H⁰(𝒪(Θᵃ − d)) ⊆ H⁰(𝒪(Θᵃ))`:

* `DivisorAdaptation.vanishingSide` / `vanishingDiv` — a global twisted pair vanishing
  along `d`, read on the piece `D(h_p)` through its pinned-chart side, and its unique
  cofactor over the adaptation equation `f_p`;
* `DivisorAdaptation.vanishingToGlued` — **the backward junction**: the cofactor family
  is a matched family of the theta-ideal datum (transition units `(f_q/f_p)·θ^{±a}`) —
  a global section of the datum sheaf, with NO sheaf gluing (datum sections are
  definitionally matched families);
* `DivisorAdaptation.gluedVanishingFst/Snd`, `gluedToVanishing` — **the forward
  junction**: the two chart assemblies `gluedToIdeal₀/₁` of a global datum section form
  a twisted pair vanishing along `d`.

The junction equivalence `gluedEquivVanishing`/`datumH0EquivVanishing` (mutually
inverse by uniqueness of cofactors) and the engine transport (`datumRigidEngine` ⟹
`K_a(d)`/`divisorWindow` finite projective over a Noetherian test ring, given the
fibrewise `h¹`-data of the theta-ideal datum) are in
`AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivSchemeCertificateEngine` (the 500-line cap).

Everything is stated for an arbitrary adaptation, so the DDR-3 universal family
(`ThetaGeneratorSeed.divisorAdaptation`) and DD-4's Task-4 residual both consume it.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false
set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false

universe u

open CategoryTheory Limits TopologicalSpace Opposite

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra

variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))} {R : Type u} [CommRing R]
  [Algebra k R]
variable {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsFinite π]

namespace DivisorAdaptation

variable {d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations} {A : DivisorAdaptation C R π d} {a : ℕ}

/-- Restriction of scheme sections commutes with the `Scheme.overModule` action. -/
private lemma resHom_smul {V W : (relCurve C R).Opens} (h : V ≤ W) (r : R)
    (s : Γ(relCurve C R, W)) :
    (relCurve C R).resHom h (r • s) = r • (relCurve C R).resHom h s := by
  rw [Scheme.overModule_smul_def, map_mul, Scheme.overModule_smul_def]
  congr 1
  exact (relCurve C R).overAlgebraMap_apply_res R (homOfLE h).op r

/-! ## The backward junction: from a vanishing pair to a global datum section -/

section Backward

variable (x : ↥(d.vanishingSubmodule R (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀
    (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁ (relThetaCocycle C R π a)))

variable (A a) in
/-- **The side reading of a vanishing pair on a piece**: the pinned-chart component of
the pair on the part of the chart cut by `⊤ ⊓ D(h_p)`. -/
noncomputable def vanishingSide : ∀ p : A.index, Γ(relCurve C R, ⊤ ⊓ A.pieces p)
  | Sum.inl i => (relCurve C R).resHom

import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivSchemeCertZarSeed

/-!
# From pointwise away-certificates to a span-`⊤` family

`DivSchemeCertZarSeed.lean` reduced the DD-R certificate gate to *away-local* certificates
over a span-`⊤` family.  The geometry that produces such certificates, however, is
pointwise on the base: the support tube (`Scheme.LocalEquations.exists_supportTube`)
isolates the pieces over a Zariski neighbourhood **of one base point at a time**, and the
fibre analyses all read at a single `p : PrimeSpectrum R`.

This file closes that gap with the quasi-compactness step.  If for every prime `p` there
is some `r ∉ p` over whose away localization the system is certified, then the good
elements span the unit ideal (their basic opens cover `Spec R`), so finitely many of them
already do — and `isLocallyCertified_of_forall_exists_away` applies.

The result is that the certificate gate for the DD-R endgame is now genuinely *pointwise*:
one base point at a time, exactly the shape the landed fibre machinery delivers.

## Main declarations

* `AlgebraicGeometry.isLocallyCertified_of_forall_prime_exists_away` — the pointwise gate
  for a bare local-equation system.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.ThetaGeneratorSeed.isLocallyCertified_of_forall_prime_away_certified`
  — the seed form.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false
set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false
set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3

universe u

open CategoryTheory Limits TopologicalSpace Opposite

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra

/-! ## The quasi-compactness step -/

section SpanTop

variable {R : Type u} [CommRing R]

/-- **Pointwise good elements span the unit ideal, finitely.** If a predicate `P` on `R`
holds at some element outside each prime, then finitely many elements satisfying `P` span
`⊤`.  This is quasi-compactness of `Spec R` in the elementary form the certificate gate
needs: the basic opens of the good elements cover the spectrum, hence the good set spans
the unit ideal, hence `1` is a finite combination of good elements. -/
theorem exists_fin_span_eq_top_of_forall_prime (P : R → Prop)
    (h : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum R, ∃ r, r ∉ p.asIdeal ∧ P r) :
    ∃ (m : ℕ) (g : Fin m → R), Ideal.span (Set.range g) = ⊤ ∧ ∀ i, P (g i) := by
  classical
  -- the good elements span the unit ideal, because their basic opens cover `Spec R`
  have hspan : Ideal.span {r : R | P r} = ⊤ := by
    rw [← PrimeSpectrum.iSup_basicOpen_eq_top_iff']
    refine top_le_iff.mp fun p _ => ?_
    obtain ⟨r, hrp, hrP⟩ := h p
    exact Opens.mem_iSup.mpr ⟨r, by
      simpa only [Opens.mem_iSup, PrimeSpectrum.mem_basicOpen] using ⟨hrP, hrp⟩⟩
  -- `1` is then a finite combination of good elements

The universal seed's RD-N (`SeedUnivRDN`, `DivSchemeRedesignSeedUniv.lean`) is the threaded
hypothesis of `seedUniv'` / `isGenerator_seedUniv'`: at every point `z`, the seed colength
`seedUnivColength z = chartColengthModule K_univ (side z) (sec z)` avoids the module-stalk prime
of `z`.

This file packages the κ(z) reduction chain (`DivSchemeRedesignKappaZ.lean`) at the seed level:
`SeedUnivRDN` follows from the **single honest input** — seed-level germ divisibility

  `∀ z, ∀ ψ ∈ K_univ, germ_z (read ψ) ∈ ⟨germ_z (read (sec z))⟩`   (in the stalk `𝒪_z`),

i.e. the achiever's `read sec z` (which attains the base multiplicity at `z`, I-0291, hence has
minimal order in the fibre DVR at `z`) locally generates the readings at `z`.  This is exactly
the achiever's per-point local-generation, base-changed to the total-space germ — the remaining
geometric content (I-0305 §route step 2 (ii), the fibre-DVR → germ transport) isolated to one
seed-level germ-divisibility premise.

`seedUnivRDN_of_forall_germ_mem_span` discharges `SeedUnivRDN` from that premise via the
per-point germ reduction `notMem_support_chartColengthModule_of_forall_germ_mem_span` and the
window finiteness `finite_divUniversalSeedK`.  Single-point throughout — the degree obstruction
(I-0305 §2, which kills the *global* κ(p) base-fibre) never fires.  Certificate-free,
`IsGenerator`-free.
-/

import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivSchemeCertSeed
import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivisorFamilyZarMapAlg

/-!
# Zariski-local certification of a seed system: relaxing the global certificate gate

The DD-R endgame consumes divisor families through `DivFamZar` (`DivisorFamilyZar.lean`),
whose membership predicate is `IsLocallyCertified`: some span-`⊤` family `g : Fin m → R`
carries certified families over the localizations `Localization.Away (g i)` which are
divisor-equal to the pulled system.  **Nothing downstream of `DivFamZar` asks for a
certificate over `R` itself.**

The certificate-assembly lane has nevertheless been attacking the *global* clause
`(D.divisorAdaptation hD).IsCertified g` over the chart ring `R_Z`, whose no-leak input
is exactly the hypothesis that is FALSE for arbitrary extracted pieces (I-0209: a piece
whose support trace leaks has a non-finite colength, and the localization repair breaks
finiteness over `R`).  The lane has been paying for a strictly stronger statement than
its consumer needs.

This file lands the relaxation.  `isLocallyCertified_of_forall_exists_away` says: to
certify a system *Zariski-locally* it suffices to produce, for each member of some
span-`⊤` family, a certified family over that localization which is divisor-equal to the
pulled system.  Then `ThetaGeneratorSeed.isLocallyCertified_of_forall_away_isCertified`
specializes it to a seed: if the seed's adaptation acquires a certificate **after
localizing at each member of a span-`⊤` family** — which is precisely what the support
tube produces (`Scheme.LocalEquations.exists_supportTube`: piece isolation is available
Zariski-locally on the base, never globally) — then the seed's own system is locally
certified, and hence has a `DivFamZar` class.

The mathematical content is the observation that `IsLocallyCertified` is designed to be
produced from local data and that the seed's pulled system over an away localization is
`DivEq` to the pulled adaptation's system on the nose; the localization step that makes
no-leak true is licensed here rather than being an unrecoverable obstruction.

## Main declarations

* `AlgebraicGeometry.isLocallyCertified_of_forall_exists_away` — the span-`⊤` production
  rule for `IsLocallyCertified`, stated with `Localization.Away` charts.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.ThetaGeneratorSeed.isLocallyCertified_of_forall_away_certified` —
  the seed form: away-local certificates give a locally certified seed system.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.ThetaGeneratorSeed.divFamZar_of_forall_away_certified` — the
  resulting `DivFamZar` class, the object every DD-R consumer actually wants.
-/

consumer (`divRepPullAt`, `DivRepAffinePullback.pull`, `divRepClassifyZar`) actually
takes as input.  No global `IsCertified` over `R` is required. -/

    {m : ℕ} (g : Fin m → R) (hg : Ideal.span (Set.range g) = ⊤)

globally certified seed is locally certified.  Recorded so that the relaxation is a
genuine weakening of the old gate rather than a parallel track. -/

    (hc : (D.divisorAdaptation hD).IsCertified n) :
    IsLocallyCertified C R pi n (D.localEquations hD) := by

/-!
# No-leak over a shrunken base, with no fibre hypothesis

The certificate assemblers consume, per piece `j`, the fibrewise clause

`∀ s, (fibre over s) ∩ closure (supp ∩ pieces j) ⊆ pieces j`

(`isCertified_of_noLeak_kernel_spanning`), equivalently emptiness of the **leak locus**
`supportLeak (pieces j) = closure (supp ∩ pieces j) \ pieces j`
(`Scheme.LocalEquations.isClosed_supportLocus_inter_iff_supportLeak_eq_empty`).

The `tube-fibre` leaf of the DD-R lane tried to obtain this by putting the whole support
inside a single piece.  That shape is refuted — `DivSchemeCertZarSep.lean`,
`not_exists_unique_support_piece`: both pinned charts carry a partition of unity, so a
support point of `V₀ ⊓ V₁` always lies in two distinct pieces.

This file gets the clause a different way, and **without any fibre analysis**.  The leak
locus is closed, and under a universally closed structure morphism its base image is closed
too (`isClosed_image_supportLeak`).  So:

* over the *open complement* of that base image, nothing leaks;
* that complement is a Zariski neighbourhood of every base point it contains, refinable to a
  basic open — the `Localization.Away` shape the pointwise gate consumes.

The leak locus is a genuine obstruction only over its own base image, which is a **closed**
subset of `Spec R`. So the no-leak clause is available on a Zariski-dense open of the base
for free; what a fibre analysis is still needed for is the base points *inside* that closed
image.

## Main declarations

* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.LocalEquations.exists_basicOpen_supportLeak_eq_empty` — a basic
  open around any base point outside the leak's image, over which nothing leaks.
* `Scheme.LocalEquations.forall_fibre_closure_subset_of_supportLeak_inter_eq_empty` —
  leak-freeness over an open of the base gives the assembler's fibrewise clause there.
-/

/-!
# The support tube in `Away`-chart form

The pointwise certificate gate (`DivSchemeCertZarPointwise.lean`) asks, at each base prime
`p`, for an element `r ∉ p` such that the pulled system is certified over
`Localization.Away r`.  The support tube (`Scheme.LocalEquations.exists_supportTube`)
delivers piece isolation over an *abstract* Zariski neighbourhood `V` of `p`.  This file
refines that neighbourhood to a basic open — the shape `Localization.Away` needs — and
records the resulting statement.

The refinement is the standard fact that basic opens form a topological basis of
`Spec R` (`PrimeSpectrum.isBasis_basic_opens`); the content is only that the tube's
conclusion is monotone in the neighbourhood, so shrinking `V` to a basic open inside it
preserves support isolation.

## Main declarations

* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.LocalEquations.exists_basicOpen_supportTube` — the tube with a
  basic-open neighbourhood: an `r ∉ p` whose basic open isolates the support inside `U`.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_notMem_supportLocus_subset_of_fibre` — the same for the
  relative curve over a test ring, with the properness licence supplied.
-/

variable {X : Scheme.{u}} {R : Type u} [CommRing R] (d : X.LocalEquations)

/-- **The support tube with a basic-open neighbourhood.** If the support fibre over a base
prime `p` lies inside an open `U`, then some `r ∉ p` has its whole basic-open preimage's
support inside `U`.

The tube produces an abstract neighbourhood; basic opens are a basis of `Spec R`
(`PrimeSpectrum.isBasis_basic_opens`), so shrinking to a basic open inside it keeps the
conclusion by monotonicity of the preimage. This is the form the `Localization.Away`
charts of `IsLocallyCertified` consume. -/
theorem exists_basicOpen_supportTube (f : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of R))
    [UniversallyClosed f] {U : Set X} (hU : IsOpen U) {p : PrimeSpectrum R}
    (hfib : f.base ⁻¹' {(p : Spec (CommRingCat.of R))} ∩ d.supportLocus ⊆ U) :
    ∃ r : R, r ∉ p.asIdeal ∧
      f.base ⁻¹' (PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen r : Set (PrimeSpectrum R))
        ∩ d.supportLocus ⊆ U := by
  obtain ⟨V, hpV, hV⟩ := d.exists_supportTube f hU hfib
  -- refine `V` to a basic open around `p`
  obtain ⟨W, hWmem, hpW, hWV⟩ :=
    PrimeSpectrum.isTopologicalBasis_basic_opens.exists_subset_of_mem_open
      (a := p) hpV V.isOpen
  obtain ⟨r, rfl⟩ := hWmem
  exact ⟨r, (PrimeSpectrum.mem_basicOpen r p).mp hpW,
    fun x hx => hV ⟨hWV hx.1, hx.2⟩⟩

/-!
# The certificate of a support-separated adaptation

The DD-R certificate lane was built around the equalizer `W(d) = ker (δ_left − δ_right)`
of the two overlap-restriction arrows.  Its two flat-cokernel clauses (c3)/(c4), and the
kernel-spanning input of `isCertified_of_noLeak_kernel_spanning`, are the genuinely hard
relative content — `DivSchemeHighWindowSyzygy.lean` shows the kernel-spanning law is
*equivalent* to the flatness one is trying to prove, so no cleverer submodule evades it.

This file records the escape hatch that the *pointwise* gate opens up.  Because
`isLocallyCertified_of_forall_prime_exists_certified_adaptation` accepts **any**
adaptation over the shrunken base, we are free to choose one whose pieces are
**support-separated**: each off-diagonal overlap misses the divisor, so its overlap
colength vanishes.  For such an adaptation

* `δ_left = δ_right` on the nose (`deltaLeft_eq_deltaRight_of_separated`), hence
* `W(d)` is the whole product `∏_j colength j` (`gluedSubmodule_eq_top_of_separated'`), and
* both cokernels are *zero* modules, so (c3)/(c4) hold for free
  (`flat_coker_incl_of_separated`, `flat_coker_diff_of_separated`).

What remains of the certificate is only the (c1) data — chart-local colengths finite
projective — plus the constant-rank reading of their product.  Both are already available:
(c1) from the support tube (`SupportTubeFinite.lean`, `SupportTube.lean`) and the rank as a
sum of the per-piece ranks (`Module.rankAtStalk_pi`).

This is a genuine reduction, not a repackaging: the hypothesis it trades for is the
*geometric separation* of the chosen pieces, which the tube produces one base point at a
time, whereas the discharged hypotheses were fibrewise flatness statements over a
nonreduced base.

## Main declarations

* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivisorAdaptation.gluedSubmodule_eq_top_of_separated'` — the equalizer
  collapses over an arbitrary base ring (the field-level lemma generalized).
* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivisorAdaptation.deltaLeft_eq_deltaRight_of_separated` — the Čech
  difference vanishes.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivisorAdaptation.isCertified_of_separated` — the certificate from
  (c1) plus a rank reading, with no kernel-spanning and no flatness input.
-/
